alerts.title: Abdominal pain requires ADR screening and reporting
alerts.message: Guidelines require all health workers to screen every patient encounter for suspected adverse drug reactions using the Drug Safety Screening checklist, and all suspected ADRs, whether mild or severe, must be recorded in HMIS tools and reported. The patient reports abdominal pain with no fever and preserved appetite while on TDF, 3TC, and DTG. The clinician's plan documents the symptom but does not include an ADR assessment, aDSM form completion, or reporting. Non-drug causes such as dietary factors or intercurrent illness should also be considered, but the symptom has not been formally evaluated as a possible drug reaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete the Drug Safety Screening checklist for this abdominal pain, assess for drug attribution, record findings in ART card/eMRS, and submit aDSM form to NDA if an ADR is suspected.
